pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to the venta-protocol-v2-device library: what it does, who it is for, how it fits into the Venta device ecosystem, and links to child pages for deeper detail.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Step-by-step guide for installing the package, locating your device IP address, and running the first status query. Covers pip install, local (editable) install, and the quick-start code example.

pages.title: Device Discovery and Network Requirements
pages.purpose: Explains why Protocol V2 does not support UDP-based auto-discovery (unlike V3), how to find the device IP, and best practices for DHCP reservations to ensure stable addressing.

pages.title: Core Library Architecture
pages.purpose: Overview of the venta_protocol_v2_device Python package internals: the single-class design, the /datastructure HTTP endpoint, the request/response lifecycle, and links to child pages covering the API and data model in detail.

pages.title: Venta_Protocol_v2_Device Class — Public API
pages.purpose: Detailed reference for every public method of the Venta_Protocol_v2_Device class: constructor, getStatus(), toJSON(), all set* control methods, and runUpdate(). Includes parameter types, return values, and side-effects.

pages.title: Device State Model and Data Categories
pages.purpose: Documents all instance attributes populated by getStatus() and _processResponse(), organized into the four hardware data blocks (Header, Action, Info, Measure) plus the derived DaysToService field. Explains how raw /datastructure JSON maps to Python attributes.

pages.title: Internal Methods and Communication Layer
pages.purpose: Covers the private implementation details: _makeCall(), _setAction(), _processResponse(), _walkProperties(), and the three _require_* type-validation helpers. Explains the HTTP POST flow to /datastructure, timeout handling, and error propagation.

pages.title: Usage Examples
pages.purpose: Overview of the practical usage resources included in the repository, linking to child pages for the Jupyter notebook walkthrough and usage tips.

pages.title: Jupyter Notebook Walkthrough
pages.purpose: Detailed guide to usage/basic_device_control.ipynb: how to run it, what each cell demonstrates (instantiation, getStatus output structure, each control method, type-error handling), and how to adapt it for real devices.

pages.title: Home Automation and Scripting Patterns
pages.purpose: Practical patterns for integrating the library into automation workflows: polling loops, error handling for offline devices, logging, and comparison with the venta_protocol_v3_device API for migration.

pages.title: Packaging and Distribution
pages.purpose: Overview of how the library is packaged and published, linking to child pages for build configuration and PyPI release process.

pages.title: Build Configuration
pages.purpose: Documents pyproject.toml and setup.py: project metadata (name, version, license, authors), Python version requirements, the requests dependency pin, setuptools build backend, and the egg-info metadata files.

pages.title: PyPI Release and Distribution Artifacts
pages.purpose: Explains the publish.yml GitHub Actions workflow that builds and uploads the package to PyPI on release events, the OIDC trusted-publishing mechanism, and the dist/ wheel and sdist artifacts.

pages.title: CI/CD and Repository Automation
pages.purpose: Overview of the three GitHub Actions workflows and supporting configuration that automate quality checks, documentation deployment, and dependency management.

pages.title: CodeQL Security Analysis
pages.purpose: Details the codeql.yml workflow: triggers (push/PR to main), path filters, the Python CodeQL matrix, autobuild step, docs/ exclusion, and how results surface in the GitHub Security tab.

pages.title: Documentation Deployment Pipeline
pages.purpose: Explains the deploy-pages.yml workflow: Jekyll build from docs/, artifact management to avoid duplicates, GitHub Pages deployment, and the manual workflow_dispatch trigger.

pages.title: Dependency Management and Repository Governance
pages.purpose: Covers the Dependabot configuration for automated dependency updates, the CODEOWNERS file assigning @tonyjurg as reviewer, and the .gitignore patterns.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.purpose: Definitions of all codebase-specific terms, protocol concepts, attribute names, and abbreviations that an onboarding engineer needs to understand when working with this library. Each entry includes code pointers.
